description_en: Kavīndrapura is probably the only temple of a grand size dedicated to Nāsaḥdyaḥ, the deity of music and drama who is invariably represented only by a small triangular hole on a wall.Constructed in 1657 CE (NS 777) by King Pratāpa Malla, it used to be one of the tallest structures in the Kathmandu Durbar Square. Architecturally, Kavīndrapura has elements of both a temple andsataḥ. The three-tiered rectangular structure has traditional tiles laid on its roofs with three finials on top. The west-facing structure has its ground floor arcaded with altogether 13 bays; seven bays in the middle protrude by about two meters from the rest. The topmost tier is built only on the protruding section, which makes it appear like a balconied tower (pula). A photo of Kavīndrapura taken before the 1934 earthquakes shows an additional tier on top. A statue of Nāsaḥdyaḥ is enshrined as the main deity on the ground floor along with other deities like Bhṛṅgī, Narasiṃha, Cāmuṇḍā, along with some statues of unidentifiable deities. Locally, the temple is known more as the Nāsaḥdyaḥ shrine than Kavīndrapura. Similar to asataḥ, the upper floor is an open hall that allows a large number of people to gather. In the chronicles, the king is said to have established a statue of Nāsaḥdyaḥ in a newly-builtphalcāthat he named ‘Madu-nāsālā-deva’ (lit. Nāsaḥdyaḥ of the Maruṭola) (Wright 1877, p.214).Two large inscriptions at Kavīndrapura reveal that it was built by King Pratāpa Malla in 1657 CE (NS 777). The inscriptions state that Narasiṃha, the fourth incarnation of Lord Viṣṇu, got infuriated when the king danced in the guise of the deity. To appease Narasiṃha, Pratāpa Malla built Kavīndrapura and enshrined a statue of Narasiṃha along with various other tantric deities (G. Vajrācārya VS 2033, p.51). The portion with the date in the inscription has already eroded. Hence, the date is no longer legible in the inscription. Although G. Vajrācārya (VS 2033, p.50) mentions the temple of Nāsaḥdyaḥ later came to be known as Kavīndrapura. However, it is clear from the two inscriptions here that the building was named Kavīndrapura by Pratāpa Malla himself at the time of its construction. Pratāpa Malla features in many of his inscriptions with the titlekavīndra(lit. king of poets). He further mentions in the inscription that a statue of Narasiṃha was also established here along with a statue of Nṛtyeśvara, the Sanskrit name of Nāsaḥdyaḥ, as the building was constructed with a special focus on the performance of dances. Nāsaḥdyaḥ is seen in the company of Śiva’s dancing attendants Bhṛṅgi and Nṛtyeśvarī, along with his animal mount Nandī. The shrine on the top level is dedicated to Bhavānīśaṅkara, thevaiṣṇavatriad of Jagannātha, Subhadrā, and Balabhadra, in which Jagannātha represents Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa in the company of his brother and sister (Gutschow 2011, p.512).Kavīndrapura collapsed in the 1934 earthquakes and was never rebuilt into its original structure. Only three roofs survive as the top two floors collapsed in the 1934 earthquake. Recent encroachments have eliminated the arcade and the balcony in the back, a repair scheme undertaken by the Department of Archaeology renewed the roofing and the walls of the side wings in 1986 (Gutschow 2011, p.512). Gutschow (2011, p.512-513) has published acomparative viewof the original Kavīndrapura built by Pratāpa Malla and the one reconstructed after the 1934 earthquakes. The Hanumandhoka Durbar Square Conservation Program of the Kathmandu Metropolis renovated Kavīndrapura at a cost of NRs. 1.76 million (J. Sāha VS 2068, online). The shops on the ground floor were vacated and thephalcāwas closed with wooden enclosures designed like latticed windows. Apaintingof Kavīndrapura by Henry A. Oldfield from 1857 CE with shops on its ground floor is evidence that thephalcāon the ground floor was already rented out to shops back then.Currently (April 2023), a lady from the Śākya caste performs the daily rituals here at the Nāsaḥdyaḥ shrine on the ground floor of Kavīndrapura. In the course of training a new batch of students of traditional musical instruments and dance, the residents of Kvaḥne, the southern part of the city of Kathmandu, customarily visit Nāsaḥdyaḥ of Kavīndrapura for worship at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end of the training. After the conclusion of the training, Nāsaḥdyaḥ is worshipped with a sacrifice of a he-goat. All the traditional musical ensembles that pass by Kavīndrapura must perform a special tune in praise of Nāsaḥdyaḥ. Such performance of a special tune is known asdyaḥlhāygu. Once every 12 years, the mask dances of Bhadrakālī from Naradevī and Khokanā are exhibited in front of Kavīndrapura. During the exhibition, the dance troupe stays in the open space on the upper floor of Kavīndrapura. The upper floor appears to have been made open to be used for such causes.
description_ne: प्रताप मल्लले बनाएको यो संरचना तत्कालीन समयका उचो मन्दिरहरू मध्येको एक थियो । प्राय खोपी बनाई सानो देवस्थल (shrine) मा स्थापना गरिएको पाइनेनासःद्यःलाई यहाँ भने भव्य मन्दिर बनाइएको पाइनुलाई पृथक उदाहरण मान्न सकिन्छ ।काठमाडौं दरबार क्षेत्रको दक्षिण-पश्चिम भागमा भएका सतः आकारका भव्य सम्पदाहरूमध्ये यो पनि एक हो । वास्तुका दृष्टिले कवीन्द्रपुर एक पृथक अभ्यासबाट बनाइएको देखिन्छ । आयताकार परम्परागत पेगोडा संरचनामा कूल १३ कवल निकालिएका छन् जसमध्ये बीचका सात कवलको मोहोडा भाग पेटीदेखि नै करिब दुई मीटर अगाडि सारी त्यसमाथि अग्लो मन्दिर उठाइएको छ । मध्य भागमा भएको यसै वास्तु स्वरूपमा कीर्तिपुर र भक्तपुरको भैरव मन्दिरहरू बनेका छन् । मन्दिरको रूप दिन बीचको यस भाग (सात कवल) लाई तीन तलामा उठाई झिंगटीको छाना हालिएको छ । विसं १९९० (सन् १९३४) को भूकम्पपूर्व खिचिएको फोटोमा तेस्रो तलाको छानामाथि थप एकपुरनिकाली तीनवटा गजूर हालिएको देख्न सकिन्छ । यसरी यो काठमाडौंमा भएका अग्ला पेगोडा शैलीका सम्पदामध्ये एक हुने गर्दथ्यो । भूमि तलाको मध्य कवलभित्र मुख्य देवताका रूपमानासःद्यःहालिएको छ । मूल मूर्तिका रूपमानासःद्यःभएकै कारण बोलीचालीमा कवीन्द्रपुर भन्दा यो सम्पदालाई बुझाउननासःद्यःको व्यापक प्रयोग भएको पाउँछौं ।नासःद्यःनेवार समाजमा नृत्य, वाद्य एवं कला विधाको देवताका रूपमा पुजिन्छन् र हरेक बस्तीमानासःद्यःअनिवार्य स्थापना गरिएको पाउँछौं । प्राय खोपी र सानो देवस्थल (shrine) का रूपमा मात्र स्थापना गरिएको पाइनेनाःसद्यःकोयो मन्दिर (कवीन्द्रपुर) एक मात्र भव्य संरचना हो ।नासःद्यःका साथमा अन्य देवदेवीका मूर्ति पनि भए तापनिनासःद्यःलाई मूलदेवता मानी स्थापना गरिएको यो मन्दिरको माथिल्लो तलालाई खुला हल (सभाकक्ष) को आकार दिइएको छ । ठुलो संख्यामा मानिस अट्ने स्वरूपमा बनाइएको यो मौलिक संरचना कला सम्बन्धी गतिविधिहरू जस्तै वाद्य, नाच वा अन्य सम्मेलन गर्ने हेतुले बनेको प्रतीत हुन्छ । भूमि तलामा फल्चा र माथिल्लो तला सतः/चपाः जस्तै मानिसको जमघट भई सामाजिक कार्य गरिने भएकै कारण सम्भवतः यसलाई बोलीचालीमा मन्दिर(देगः)नभनिएको हो । जनबोलीमानासःद्यःर कवीन्द्रपुर पाछाडि मन्दिर वा देगः जोडिएको देखिदैन । राईटको वंशावलीमा पनि मन्दिर नभनी राजालेनासःद्यःको मूर्ति बनाई नवनिर्मित पाटीमा राखेको र 'मदु-नासाला-देव' नाम राखेको भनिएको छ (Wright 1877, p.214) ।यस भव्य संरचनाको निर्माण राजा प्रताप मल्लले गरेको कुरा यही भएको अभिलेखमा जनाइएको छ । दुई ठुला आकारका संस्कृत र नेवार भाषामा लिखित यी अभिलेखमा प्रताप मल्ल स्वयं नरसिंह भई नाच्दै गर्दा नृत्यस्थलको वेदिकाबाट नरसिंह भगवान आक्रोशित भई विचित्रको आवाज निस्केकाले शान्त पार्न नरसिंहका साथै अन्य तान्त्रिक देवदेवी स्थापना गरी यो कवीन्द्रपुर बनाइएको भनिएको छ (G. Vajrācārya VS 2033, p.51) । रोचक प्रकृतिको विवरण दिने यस अभिलेखमा मिति कुँदिएको भाग दुर्भाग्यवस् खिइसकेको छ । प्रताप मल्ल अनेकन विषयमा दखल भएका एक महत्वाकांक्षी राजाका रूपमा इतिहासमा प्रसिद्ध छन् । उनी आफू कवि भएकोमा ठुलो आत्मगौरव थियो भन्ने तथ्य पुष्टि हुने विविध उदाहरणहरू पाइन्छन् । उनले कवीन्द्र उपाधि लिएका थिए र हरेक अभिलेखमा आफ्नो कवीन्द्र उपनाम प्रयोग गरेका छन् । महेन्द्र मल्लले चलाएको मुद्रा 'महेन्द्रमल्ली' कहलियो तर प्रताप मल्लको टक 'प्रताप'का आधारमा नभई 'कवीन्द्रमल्ली' का रूपमा प्रसिद्ध हुनुले उनको कवि व्यक्तित्वको प्रभाव झल्कन्छ । उनले हनुमानढोकाको जगन्नाथ मन्दिर (KAT1740) मा १४ लिपिमा श्लोक लेखाई आफ्नो कवित्वको छाप छोड्ने चेष्टा गरेका थिए । यस्तै महत्वाकांक्षी अभ्यासका रूपमा उनले यस भव्य संरचनालाई 'कवीन्द्रपुर' नाम दिएको देखिन्छ । G. Vajrācārya (VS 2033, p.50) ले 'नासलदेवताको मन्दिरको नाम कवीन्द्रपुर रहन गएको छ'  भनेका छन् तर यो नाम निर्मातालाई जोडी पछि मात्र रहन गएको नभै प्रताप मल्ल स्वंयले इच्छाएर राखेको कुरा अभिलेखबाटै खुल्दछ । अभिलेखमै आफ्नो नामको कवीन्द्रपुरमा नरसिंहको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको, नृत्यकलालाई लक्षित गरिएको हुनाले साथमा नन्दी, महाकाल सहित नृत्येश्वर, भवानीशंकर, जगन्नाथ, भगवती, गणेश पनि स्थापना गरियो भनिएको छ । राजा स्वंयमले श्लोक लेखी अभिलेखमा कुँदाएको कुरा अभिलेखमा परेको छ ।यो भव्य संरचना विसं १९९० (सन् १९३४) मा भत्केपश्चात् पुरानै आकारमा उठ्न सकेन । माथिल्लोपुरभएको तलालाई होचो बनाईपुरथपिएन । उक्त भूकम्प अघि र पछिको तुलनात्मक नक्शा Gutschwo (2011, p.512-13/drawing) ले प्रकाशमा ल्याएका छन् । काठमाडौं महानगरपालिका अन्तर्गत हनुमानढोका दरबार क्षेत्र संरक्षण कार्यक्रम शीर्षकमा विसं २०६८ (सन् २०११) मा रू १७ लाख ६८ हजार खर्चेर कवीन्द्रपुरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो (J. Sāha VS 2068,online) । यसै ताका भूमि तलाको फल्चामा भएका पसलहरूलाई हटाई आँखीझ्यालजस्तो देखिने काष्ठफलकले सम्पूर्ण कवलहरू बन्द गरिएको हो । सन् १८५७ मा Oldfield ले कोरेको जलरङ्ग चित्रमा भूमि तलाका कवलहरू पसलका रूपमा प्रयोग भएको देखिएकाले यहाँ पसल राख्ने थिति निकै पुरानो हो भन्ने खुल्दछ (चित्र हेर्नुहोस्) ।यहाँ हाल (अप्रिल २०२३)नासःद्यःको नित्यपूजा शाक्य थरकी स्थानीय महिलाले गर्दै आएकी छिन् । काठमाडौंको कोने (दक्षिणी खण्ड) मा बाद्यवादन, नृत्य आदिको प्रशिक्षणको प्रारम्भ, मध्यावधि र समापनमा कवीन्द्रपुरकानासःद्यःलाई विशेष पूजा गर्नुपर्ने थिति यद्यपि कायम छ । प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रमको समापनपछि बलि सहितनासःद्यःपूजी बलिको सिङ टाग्ने चलन छ । कवीन्द्रपुर हुँदै जाने कुनैपनि सांगीतिक झाँकीले यस मन्दिर अगाडि रुकीनासःद्यःको नाममा धुन अर्पण गर्नुपर्न (द्यः ल्हाय्‌गु/सलामी) अनिवार्य मानिन्छ । १२ वर्षमा एकपल्ट कवीन्द्रपुरको ठीक अगाडि नरदेवीको भद्रकाली र खोकनाको नृत्य नचाउने चलन छ । काठमाडौं दरबार क्षेत्रमा नाच नसकुन्जेलको अवधि नृत्यटोली कवीन्द्रपुरकै माथिल्लो तलामा वास वस्ने चलन छ । यस चलनबाट पनि यो संरचना खासगरी बाद्य र नृत्य अभ्यासको हेतु बनाइएको हो भनी अनुमान हुन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Two large inscriptions in Sanskrit and Newari record the construction of Kavīndrapura by King Pratāpa Malla. The inscriptions state that Narasiṃha, the fourth incarnation of Lord Viṣṇu, got infuriated when the king danced in the guise of the deity. To appease Narasiṃha, Pratāpa Malla built Kavīndrapura and enshrined a statue of Narasiṃha along with various other deities.

King Pratapa Malla recorded the endowment of many plots of land in the name of the deities enshrined in Kavīndrapura in this inscription. He also outlined various rituals and traditions to be carried out from the income of the lands.

Siddhi Tāmrākāra and others from Garakuta, the courtyard in front (west) of Kavīndrapura now known as Gaḥkuti, endowed land to set up a trust (guthi) in the name of Dvibhujasamvara, their lineage deity.

This inscription from the Rāṇā period is currently (April 2023) placed here in Kavīndrapura but is not related to the monument. It records the establishment of the Vaikuṇṭheśvara temple and other structures in a village named Sipāduyā (?) by Vīradhvaja Kārkī and his wife Bhaktakumārī. It also records the couple endowing 31ropanīs of land to set up a trust for observing the anniversary and other periodic rituals. The inscription appears to be from some village on the foothill of the Kathmandu valley and was probably placed here on the ground floor of Kavīndrapura.

historical_events.event_name: Collapse of the top two roofs
historical_events.event_description: The upper two roofs collapsed in the 1934 earthquakes.
Recent encroachments have eliminated the arcade and the balcony in the back. A repair scheme undertaken by the Department of Archaeology renewed the roofing and the walls of the side wings in 1986.

After a person named Abhimānasiṃha Khatrī intentionally destroyed the inscription installed by Vīradhvaja Kārkī in 1827 CE (VS 1883), his youngest wife Mahāmāyā petitioned Jagat Śamśera and Raṇa Uddīpa Siṃha in the Rāṇā administration and got the content of the broken inscription reinstalled on this inscription. However, the year of the installation of this inscription is erroneously given as VS 190. Therefore, the year is unclear.

The Hanumandhoka Durbar Square Conservation Program of the Kathmandu Metropolis renovated Kavīndrapura at a cost of NRs. 1.76 million (J. Sāha VS 2068,online). The shops on the ground floor were vacated and thephalcāwas closed with wooden enclosures designed like latticed windows.
